classification.difficultyReason: Apply the one-output-per-input definition directly to four finite mapping diagrams and justify each classification.

content.prompt: Which of these relations are also functions? Explain your answers.

spec.description: Two rounded sets with ordered values and five left-to-right arrows; f labels the mapping.
spec.answerVisibility: All values and arrows are permanent student-visible givens.

answer.short: Function: every input has exactly one output.
answer.worked: Each of $-2,2,-1,1,0$ has exactly one outgoing arrow. Therefore each input has one output, so $f$ is a function.

spec.description: Two rounded sets; distinct inputs share outputs through converging arrows.
spec.mathematics: -2 and 2 map to 4; -1 and 1 map to 2; 0 maps to 1.
spec.answerVisibility: All values and arrows are permanent student-visible givens.

answer.short: Function: every input has exactly one output.
answer.worked: Each input has exactly one outgoing arrow. Different inputs may share an output: $-2$ and $2$ both map to $4$, while $-1$ and $1$ both map to $2$. Thus $g$ is a function.

spec.description: Two rounded sets; preserve both outgoing arrows from 4 and from 1.
spec.mathematics: 4 maps to -2 and 2; 1 maps to -1 and 1; 0 maps to 0.
spec.answerVisibility: All values and arrows are permanent student-visible givens.

answer.short: Not a function: $x=4$ has outputs $-2$ and $2$.
answer.worked: The arrows from $4$ give the ordered pairs $(4,-2)$ and $(4,2)$. One input therefore has two outputs, so $p$ is not a function. The input $1$ also has two outputs, $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Two rounded sets with crossed arrows between the upper inputs and outputs, and two arrows from zero.
spec.mathematics: -3 and 3 each map to both -4 and 4; 0 maps to both -5 and 5.
spec.answerVisibility: All values and arrows are permanent student-visible givens.

answer.short: Not a function: $x=0$ has outputs $-5$ and $5$.
answer.worked: The arrows from $0$ give the ordered pairs $(0,-5)$ and $(0,5)$. One input therefore has two outputs, so $q$ is not a function. Each of $-3$ and $3$ also has two outputs, $-4$ and $4$.
